method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18; no REFUSE (gaps answer `not covered`, asserted); checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Customs Tariff Act 1995, Compilation No. 100, compilation date 4 July 2026 (includes amendments up to Act No. 67, 2026; register id C2026C00399, 7 volumes), as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/C2004A04997.txt. No instrument brought in: the Customs By-laws, the Customs Tariff Regulations and the Customs Act's origin and valuation rules are asked as facts.

checks.command: l4 run cta-importer.l4 ; l4 run cta-cases-importer.l4
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read.

scope: From the seat of the traveller or small importer: how a rate is found (ss 6, 7 as a fact, 9(1), 10(1), 14(1)(a), (i), 15, 16(1)(a), (b), (d), (ja)-(v), 16(5)); nine representative Schedule 3 lines (8471.30.00, 8517.13.00, 6109.10.00, 4202.21.00, 9503.00.20, 8711.60.00, 8703.80.11, 8703.80.12, 8703.80.19); Schedule 4 items 17, 18, 24, 25, 26, 28, 36, 37 with ss 8(1), 18(1); duty at an ad valorem rate (s 9). Out: the rest of Schedule 3 and the other s 16 preferences (`not covered`), the free trade schedules' tables (asked), ss 9(2), 11, 16A-16B, 17, 18A-18B, 19-19AD, 20, s 8(2), and Schedule 4 item 15 (answered by customs-act-1901/encodings/baseline-2026-10, `not covered` here).
seat: the traveller or small importer bringing goods into Australia
